reviews.text:
Please consider adding the Name and credentials of the presenter. Information source matters a lot. If a writer/storyteller talks about their “study of a pandemic” it is much less meaningful than an epidemiologist and professor at Harvard.  

Additionally please consider adding a link to the full length TedTalk related to the Short.

reviews.title: Shocked by Lack of Features
reviews.text:
Where are the Top 10 Lists? How can we filter by most viewed, highest regarded, or even alphabetically? 
When filtering, I’d love to see all the micro-topic options listed underneath the macro option. For instance, list the different disease focuses or health options under Health. Let us click on Health as a whole or let us filter Health down further into smaller groups.
And most importantly - why can we not “Add to Queue”? You want us to stay in the app correct? Let us build a list of ones we want to listen to without “saving”. Saving is a different feature. 
I know there’s good stuff in here but it’s hard for me to stay organized and spend 10 minutes looking for a 10-minute video.

reviews.title: Who”s missing from Ted… and who’s missing out?
reviews.text:
I downloaded the app because I’ve been entertained and informed by Ted Talk speakers on topics of general interest. I’m a Christian and so decided to conduct a search for speakers on Biblical topics. To my disappointment there were no talks listed by many brilliant contemporary theologians such as RC Sproul, John MacArthur, David Jeremiah, Ravi Zacharias and Oxford mathematician John Lennox. Rick Warren did come up regarding the purpose driven life, but that was it.
On the most important questions regarding life after death and answers to  the Origin, Purpose, Morality and Destiny of humanity, there are no theologians to impart insight. Inconceivable!
Expressions I used in my search were as follows:  Bible, Christianity, Theology,  Creation, Life after death and Oxford mathematicians. 
If I’ve overlooked a topic that might bring up an authority speaking on the importance of theology, and how it answers the most important question that faces every human being… please let me know. 
The app works fine as far as I explored it, and I will rate “Ted” with 3 stars for entertainment and secular information, but absent such an important topic I would not rate higher..

reviews.title: DON’T DO IT!
reviews.text:
This app makes you sign up outside of the app. It will bill you outside of the app. You will pay, forget about it, then a year later they will bill you again for $259.20. Which will come  as a surprise and you will immediately try to contact them for a refund. After all, it’s been a year since you even used the app. You will not find any kind of support for help, other than email. They don’t have a number to call. 

They will finally  respond to your email saying they can’t find your email, despite your account saying your are signed up on their website. You will immediately send the receipt of them taking your money and they will take a few days to finally respond and tell you they previously sent you an email (which you didn’t receive and how could you if they don’t have your email connected with your account?) and can only refund you HALF of the amount they took.

Total scam. Find it somewhere else. Don’t trust.

reviews.title: PLAY WHILE IN BACKGROUND
reviews.text:
Please please please allow the app to play its audio in the background. 

People may tell you that the media of choice is visual. That video killed the radio star. But how hard is it to convey a complex idea with only the visual aspect? To demonstrate how crucial language and the audio aspect is, let’s consider that only through the use of subtitles, a novel phenomenon, is conveyance of knowledge without audio even close to possible. But aren’t subtitles just a manipulated form of audio?

I guarantee I am not the only person that wants to be free to carry on with our lives while LISTENING to Ideas that Change Everything on your app. 

Thank you.

reviews.title: 10 years later, player’s still glitchy
reviews.text:
I used to have the TED app on my iPhone 10 years ago; it was glitchy, so it’s surprising to see that 10 years later, there has been little improvement with the player.
Whatever video player you all use needs to be overhauled.
Simply pulling down the control center to increase the brightness of my phone causes the video to go black—every time, but the audio still plays somehow. The website’s video also tends to go black randomly and is laggy beyond belief, no matter what device or browser I use. 
I don’t imagine I’m only one who, out of frustration with the player, stopped visiting your app and website and chose to rely on YT to watch TED videos. The think about that is one tends to forget TED videos even exist after a while. Oh well…

reviews.title: Love the app! One suggestion.
reviews.text:
I had been watching TED talks on my safari web browser and it was always glitching. The app works great and I love that it saves your progress if you don’t finish a video. I also like being able to save videos to watch later. 

My only complaint is that I can’t find a list of already watched videos. I’ve watched a bunch and when I think about one I’d like to share with someone I can’t find it. The app would be perfect with this added.
